title: Study: Dinosaurs were charbroiled after Chicxulub impact
gist: A new Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences paper argues that fine post-impact dust from the Chicxulub asteroid trapped thermal radiation and charbroiled surface life within the first hour or two, delivering 17 times the human lethal radiation dose and igniting wildfires indirectly. The authors say this rules out the volcanism-trigger alternative and makes the dust cloud, not the blast or fireball, the reason the event became a planetary catastrophe.

insights.claim: A new paper finds the Chicxulub impact produced a dust cloud that superheated the upper atmosphere and charbroiled organisms unable to take shelter, killing most life within the first hour to two rather than over years.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Reframes the K-Pg extinction as a near-instantaneous thermal event, changing which survivor traits the fossil record should show.
insights.quote: we’re in the realm where we might be essentially killing off everything within that first hour to two

insights.claim: Once fine dust was included in the models, organisms would have been hit with 17 times the lethal radiation dose for humans, enough to burn the skin of even thick-skinned dinosaurs and cause heat stroke.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A quantified lethality figure that converts a qualitative extinction story into a testable physical threshold.
insights.quote: blasted with 17 times the lethal dose of radiation for humans

insights.claim: The radiant heat was probably not enough to directly ignite wood but was more than enough to set fire to grass, lichen and pine needles, meaning the global wildfires were ignited indirectly through fine fuels.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Resolves a long-standing objection that impact heating could not start wildfires, by routing ignition through fine fuels.

insights.claim: Co-author Brandon Johnson argues the global ejection of vapor plume material, not the blast wave or fireball, is what made this a planetary catastrophe, since the latter do not travel far.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Sets the mechanism by which local impacts scale to global extinction, relevant to impact-risk modeling generally.
insights.quote: Without the dust cloud, it would have been bad. It would have killed a lot of creatures. But it wouldn’t have been a planetary catastrophe.

insights.so_what: Prior consensus underestimated the thermal pulse because it omitted the dust component entirely.

insights.claim: The authors believe their findings rule out the alternative theory that volcanic activity triggered the mass extinction with the Chicxulub impact merely delivering a final blow.

insights.claim: The Chicxulub impactor was between 11 and 81 kilometers across and released energy over a billion times greater than the atomic bombs dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki, ejecting vaporized rock and sulfates.

insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
